name: Mirza Abu Taleb Khan
what: An unemployed Lucknow revenue officer sails with a Scottish friend from Calcutta to Britain, is lionised in London as the Persian Prince, and returns overland through France, Constantinople and Iraq, writing one of the first Indian accounts of Europe.

legs.note: Waits months for a better ship and is well received by the Dutch and British.
Calls at the island on the passage north.
Lands in Ireland after a stormy passage.
Meets Sake Dean Mahomed and receives letters from Cornwallis.
Feted as the Persian Prince and meets George III.
Meets the orientalists Silvestre de Sacy and Langles.
Travels south through Lyon.
Sails along the Italian coast.
Calls at the British-held island.
Lands in Ottoman Anatolia.
Received by Sultan Selim III.
Crosses Anatolia and Kurdistan overland.
Continues down the Tigris.
Visits the shrine of Husayn.
Visits the shrine of Ali.
Takes ship for India.
Lands in British India.
Home after four and a half years; dies in 1805.

sources.cite: Mirza Abu Taleb Khan, The Travels of Mirza Abu Taleb Khan in Asia, Africa and Europe, trans. Charles Stewart, London 1810
Michael H. Fisher, Counterflows to Colonialism: Indian Travellers and Settlers in Britain 1600-1857, Delhi 2004
Wikipedia, Mirza Abu Taleb Khan

name: Alexander the Great's campaign
what: The Macedonian king leads his army from Pella across the Hellespont, through the Persian Empire to Egypt, Bactria and the Punjab, and back through the Gedrosian desert to Babylon, where he dies.

legs.note: After crossing the Hellespont, sacrifices at the tomb of Achilles.
Defeats the Persian satraps' army in a cavalry battle at the river.
Takes the city by siege and disbands most of his fleet.
Besieges the city held by Memnon of Rhodes.
Cuts the Gordian knot.
Falls ill after bathing in the Cydnus.
Routs Darius III, who flees leaving his family behind.
Builds a mole to the island city and takes it after a seven-month siege.
Takes the city after a two-month siege; is wounded.
Welcomed by the Egyptians and sacrifices to Apis.
Consults the oracle of Zeus Ammon.
Lays out his new city on the coast.
Defeats Darius decisively on the plain east of the Tigris.
The city surrenders and Mazaeus is kept as satrap.
Seizes the Persian royal treasury.
Forces the pass held by Ariobarzanes.
Loots the treasury and burns the palace.
Sends home the Greek allies and pursues Darius.
Darius is found murdered by Bessus nearby.
Philotas is tried and executed for conspiracy.
Founds a city in Arachosia during the winter march.
Founds a city before crossing the Hindu Kush.
Bessus flees across the Oxus.
Occupies the Sogdian capital.
Founds his farthest city and defeats the Scythians across the Jaxartes.
Kills Cleitus the Black at a drunken banquet.
Takes the fortress and meets Roxana, whom he marries.
Storms the mountain fortress that Heracles reputedly failed to take.
King Ambhi (Taxiles) joins him with elephants.
Defeats King Porus and his elephants.
His army refuses to go further; builds twelve altars and turns back.
Is gravely wounded by an arrow in the chest while storming the town.
Reaches the Indus delta and sails out to the Ocean.
Emerges from the Gedrosian desert after heavy losses.
Finds Cyrus's tomb plundered and has it restored.
Holds the mass weddings of Macedonians and Persian women.
Faces and quells a mutiny of his veterans.
Hephaestion dies.
Dies of fever in Nebuchadnezzar's palace aged 32.

sources.cite: Arrian, Anabasis of Alexander, trans. P. A. Brunt, Loeb 1976-83
A. B. Bosworth, Conquest and Empire: The Reign of Alexander the Great, Cambridge 1988
Donald W. Engels, Alexander the Great and the Logistics of the Macedonian Army, Berkeley 1978
Wikipedia, Wars of Alexander the Great

name: Benjamin of Tudela
what: A Navarrese Jew records the Jewish communities of the Mediterranean and Near East on a journey from Spain to Baghdad and back by way of Egypt and Sicily.

legs.note: Notes the Cyclopean walls of the old city.
Describes a community of wise men and merchants from all lands.
Praises its ancient seat of learning and three hundred Jews.
Finds Christians and Muslims trading from Egypt, Greece and Genoa.
Takes ship along the coast.
Notes Genoa's war fleet and rivalry with Pisa.
Counts some ten thousand towers in the city's houses.
Describes Pope Alexander III's Jewish steward and the ancient monuments.
Notes its famous medical school.
Crosses to Corfu.
Finds two thousand Jews, the best silk and purple weavers in Greece.
Describes Manuel I's court, Hagia Sophia and the Hippodrome.
Sails south through the islands.
Describes the city's water supply.
Notes Jewish glassmakers and sea-going merchants.
Finds about two hundred Jews dyeing cloth under the Tower of David.
Describes the Umayyad mosque.
Continues to the Euphrates.
Describes the ruins of Nineveh across the Tigris.
Praises the caliph and describes the exilarch and ten academies.
Describes the Fatimid caliph and the Nile flood measures.
Describes the Pharos and merchants from twenty-eight Christian kingdoms.
Lands in Norman Sicily.
Describes King William II's palace gardens.
Returns to Spain.

sources.cite: The Itinerary of Benjamin of Tudela, ed. and trans. Marcus Nathan Adler, London 1907
Wikipedia, Benjamin of Tudela

name: Burton and Speke's East African expedition (Speke's route)
carrier: Burton and Speke's East African expedition (Speke's route)
what: Richard Burton and John Hanning Speke march inland from Zanzibar on the caravan road to Lake Tanganyika; on the return Speke detours alone to the lake he names Victoria and claims it as the Nile's source, beginning a bitter feud.

legs.note: A preliminary coastal trip to Usambara; both fall ill.
Wait out the rains and hire Sidi Mubarak Bombay and porters.
The caravan leaves the coast.
Fever-ridden in the Kingani valley.
Pay heavy tolls to Gogo chiefs.
Rest among Arab slave and ivory traders.
First Europeans at Lake Tanganyika; Speke is half blind and later deafened by a beetle in his ear.
Paddle north by canoe and hear the Rusizi flows into, not out of, the lake.
Return to Ujiji and start back east.
Burton stays ill and writes; Speke sets off north.
Speke becomes the first European to see the lake.
Names the lake Victoria Nyanza and decides it is the Nile's source.
Burton rejects his claim; they leave with 152 porters.
Reach the Indian Ocean.
Pay off the porters amid disputes.
Speke sails ahead while Burton waits.
Speke reports first to the Royal Geographical Society, which backs a new expedition.

sources.cite: Richard F. Burton, The Lake Regions of Central Africa, London 1860
John Hanning Speke, What Led to the Discovery of the Source of the Nile, Edinburgh 1864
Tim Jeal, Explorers of the Nile, London 2011
Wikipedia, John Hanning Speke

name: Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca
what: Treasurer of Narvaez's failed conquest of Florida, he is wrecked on the Texas coast, lives six years among Native peoples, and walks with three companions across the continent to New Spain as a healer.

legs.note: Over a hundred men desert the expedition.
A hurricane destroys two ships and kills sixty men.
Winters in Cuba.
Lands; Narvaez separates the army from the ships, which are never seen again.
Finds a town of forty houses, not the rich city hoped for.
Kills the horses and builds five rafts to sail for Panuco.
Cast ashore; most survivors die over the winter.
Lives as a captive and trader in shells and skins among coastal peoples.
Escapes with Dorantes, Castillo and Esteban during the tuna harvest.
Travels west as a healer, followed by crowds from village to village.
Meets settled farming people at the Conchos-Rio Grande confluence.
Given six hundred deer hearts; sees turquoise and emeralds from the north.
Meets Spanish slave hunters, to their mutual astonishment.
Received by Melchor Diaz.
Sees governor Nuno de Guzman.
Welcomed by Viceroy Mendoza and Cortes.
Sails for Spain.
Arrives after a voyage via Havana and the Azores.

sources.cite: Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca, La Relacion (1542), ed. and trans. Rolena Adorno and Patrick Charles Pautz, Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca: His Account, His Life, and the Expedition of Panfilo de Narvaez, Lincoln 1999
Andres Resendez, A Land So Strange: The Epic Journey of Cabeza de Vaca, New York 2007
Wikipedia, Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca

name: Columbus's first voyage
what: A Genoese captain sails west for Castile with three ships, reaches the Bahamas, Cuba and Hispaniola, loses the Santa Maria, and returns via the Azores and Lisbon.

legs.note: Repairs the Pinta's rudder and re-rigs the Nina.
Takes on water and provisions and leaves the known world.
Sails into great mats of floating weed.
Lands, claims the island for Castile and meets the Lucayan Taino.
Names the second island.
Trades with islanders and sees hammocks.
Searches for gold and a king.
Believes Cuba is the Asian mainland and sends envoys inland, who see tobacco smoking.
Reaches the island he names La Isla Espanola.
Explores the island off Hispaniola's north coast.
The Santa Maria runs aground; leaves 39 men in a fort built from its timbers.
Rejoins Martin Alonso Pinzon and the Pinta.
First armed clash with natives; sails for home.
After a great storm, half the crew is arrested by the Portuguese while at prayer.
Storm-driven into the Tagus; meets King John II.
Returns to his home port.
Received by Ferdinand and Isabella with Taino captives and gold.

sources.cite: The Diario of Christopher Columbus's First Voyage to America 1492-1493, abstracted by Las Casas, trans. Oliver Dunn and James E. Kelley, Norman 1989
Samuel Eliot Morison, Admiral of the Ocean Sea, Boston 1942
Wikipedia, Voyages of Christopher Columbus

name: Cook's first voyage (Endeavour)
what: Lieutenant James Cook takes HMS Endeavour round Cape Horn to observe the transit of Venus at Tahiti, charts New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, nearly loses the ship on the Great Barrier Reef and returns via Batavia.

legs.note: Takes on wine and fresh food.
The suspicious Portuguese viceroy keeps the crew mostly on board.
Two of Banks's servants die of cold on a botanising trip.
Rounds the Horn in unusually calm weather.
Builds Fort Venus and observes the transit of Venus on 3 June.
Guided by Tupaia to the Leeward Islands.
Claims the Society Islands and refits.
Tupaia leads him south to the Austral island.
First landing in New Zealand ends with several Maori shot.
Takes on water; Tupaia talks with Maori priests.
Observes the transit of Mercury.
Explores the northern harbour.
Careens the ship and confirms New Zealand is two islands from a hilltop.
Leaves New Zealand after charting it in six months.
Sights the east coast of Australia.
Lands among the Gweagal, who resist; Banks collects plants.
Strikes the reef at night and jettisons cannon to float off.
Beaches the ship for repairs and sees kangaroos; a quarrel with the Guugu Yimithirr over turtles.
Claims the east coast for Britain.
Buys provisions on the Dutch-dominated island.
Repairs the ship; malaria and dysentery begin killing a third of the crew.
Recovers the sick.
Sails home with an East India convoy.
Anchors off Kent after nearly three years.

sources.cite: The Journals of Captain James Cook, vol. 1: The Voyage of the Endeavour 1768-1771, ed. J. C. Beaglehole, Hakluyt Society 1955
J. C. Beaglehole, The Life of Captain James Cook, London 1974
Wikipedia, First voyage of James Cook

name: Darwin's voyage on the Beagle
what: The young naturalist Charles Darwin sails as Captain FitzRoy's companion on HMS Beagle's survey of South America and around the world, spending most of five years ashore collecting fossils, rocks and animals.

legs.note: Sees a raised band of shells in the cliffs and conceives of writing a geology book.
Delighted by the rainforest, appalled by slavery.
Lives ashore at Botafogo and rides inland to a coffee estate.
Base for the Rio de la Plata survey.
Digs out fossil bones of giant extinct mammals such as Megatherium.
Sees the Fuegians and the resettlement of Jemmy Button and his companions.
Arrives just after the British reassert control.
Collects birds and rides into the interior.
Begins an overland ride across the pampas.
Meets General Juan Manuel de Rosas during his campaign against the Indigenous peoples.
Ends his ride with the gauchos.
Finds a fossil horse tooth on the Parana.
Shoots a lesser rhea, later named Rhea darwinii.
Takes boats 200 miles upriver towards the Andes.
Crosses to the Andes and falls seriously ill at Corfield's house.
Lying in a forest when the great earthquake of 20 February strikes.
Finds the city in ruins and the land raised by several feet.
Crosses the Andes by the Portillo pass; bitten by Benchuca bugs.
Rides north through the desert to rejoin the ship.
Stuck during political unrest.
Lands among lava and giant tortoises.
Camps a week collecting finches, mockingbirds and plants.
Admires the missionaries' work and the islanders' grace.
Visits the mission station at Waimate.
Rides over the Blue Mountains to Bathurst and sees a platypus.
Studies the geology of Mount Wellington.
Watches a corroboree.
Develops his theory of coral atoll formation.
Rides an elephant.
Meets the astronomer John Herschel.
Lodges near Napoleon's tomb and studies the island's geology.
FitzRoy recrosses the Atlantic to check longitudes.
Last South American stop.
Final stop before England.
Darwin leaves the ship and hurries home to Shrewsbury.

sources.cite: Charles Darwin, Journal of Researches (The Voyage of the Beagle), London 1839
Richard Darwin Keynes (ed.), Charles Darwin's Beagle Diary, Cambridge 1988
Wikipedia, Second voyage of HMS Beagle

name: Ennin
what: A Japanese Tendai monk travels with the last Japanese embassy to Tang China, studies at Wutaishan and Chang'an, survives the Huichang persecution of Buddhism and returns home on a Silla ship.

legs.note: The ship runs aground in the Yangtze mouth shallows and the party wades ashore.
Waits months while the authorities refuse him leave to go to Mount Tiantai.
The embassy hires Silla ships and sailors for the return.
Stays behind illegally at the Korean monastery founded by Chang Pogo.
Obtains travel credentials from the prefecture.
Gets his official travel permit from the regional commandery.
Studies Tiantai and the five-tone nembutsu at the holy mountain of Manjusri.
Passes the northern capital on the way south.
Receives esoteric initiations, then lives through Emperor Wuzong's anti-Buddhist purge.
Expelled as a foreign monk, travels east in lay dress.
Passes down the Bian canal route.
Denied permission to sail from here.
Silla residents help him with lodging and boats.
Goes north to look for a ship to Japan.
Lives with the Silla community waiting nearly two years for passage.
Sails along the Silla coast on Kim Chin's ship.
Lands in Kyushu after nine years abroad.
Returns to Enryaku-ji with texts, mandalas and ritual implements.

sources.cite: Ennin's Diary: The Record of a Pilgrimage to China in Search of the Law, trans. Edwin O. Reischauer, New York 1955
Edwin O. Reischauer, Ennin's Travels in T'ang China, New York 1955
Wikipedia, Ennin

name: Esteban (Estevanico)
what: An enslaved Arabic-speaking African from Azemmour survives the Narvaez disaster, crosses North America on foot with Cabeza de Vaca, then guides Fray Marcos de Niza's search for Cibola and is killed at Hawikuh.

legs.note: Sails with his master on the Narvaez expedition.
Lands with the army.
Marches north with Narvaez.
Sails west on Dorantes's raft.
Survives the wreck; enslaved by coastal peoples.
Reunited with Cabeza de Vaca.
Goes ahead as scout and interpreter, learning local languages.
Hears of rich towns to the north.
Reaches the Spanish frontier.
Passes to Viceroy Mendoza and is chosen as guide for a northern expedition.
Leaves with Fray Marcos de Niza.
Sent ahead with Native guides, signalling news by sending back crosses.
Killed by the Zuni after demanding entry to the town.

sources.cite: Rolena Adorno and Patrick Charles Pautz, Alvar Nunez Cabeza de Vaca: His Account, His Life, and the Expedition of Panfilo de Narvaez, Lincoln 1999
Dennis Herrick, Esteban: The African Slave Who Explored America, Albuquerque 2018
Fray Marcos de Niza, Relacion (1539)
Wikipedia, Estevanico

name: Francis Xavier in Asia
what: A founding Jesuit sails from Lisbon to Goa and spends a decade restlessly moving between the Fishery Coast, Malacca, the Moluccas and Japan, dying on an island off China while waiting to enter it.

legs.note: Received by King John III; sails on his 35th birthday on the Santiago.
Winters at the Portuguese station nursing the sick.
Arrives thirteen months after leaving Lisbon and preaches in the streets with a bell.
Baptises thousands of Parava pearl fishers.
Baptises Mukkuva fishing villages.
Prays at the tomb of St Thomas and decides to go east.
Preaches in the port city.
Works among the Christian villages of Amboina.
Preaches at the Portuguese fort and sultan's court.
Visits the 'islands of hope in God' despite warnings.
Meets the Japanese fugitive Anjiro, who inspires a mission to Japan.
Writes long letters to Rome and the king.
Organises the mission as superior in India.
Boards a Chinese pirate junk for Japan.
Lands with Anjiro; received by the daimyo Shimazu Takahisa.
Welcomed by Portuguese traders.
Preaches in the streets with little success.
Finds the capital ruined by war and cannot see the emperor; leaves after eleven days.
Dressed in finery with gifts, wins Ouchi Yoshitaka's permission to preach.
Received by Otomo Sorin; sails for India.
Plans an embassy to China.
Prepares the China mission.
The captain of Malacca blocks the embassy.
Waits for a smuggler to take him to Canton and dies of fever.

sources.cite: Georg Schurhammer, Francis Xavier: His Life, His Times, 4 vols, trans. M. Joseph Costelloe, Rome 1973-82
The Letters and Instructions of Francis Xavier, trans. M. Joseph Costelloe, St Louis 1992
Wikipedia, Francis Xavier

name: Gan Ying
what: Sent by General Ban Chao towards Da Qin (Rome), a Han envoy crosses Parthia to the head of the Persian Gulf and turns back when sailors warn of a long sea voyage.

legs.note: Leaves the Tarim Basin westwards over the Pamirs.
Enters Anxi (Parthia) at its eastern frontier city.
Passes the Parthian royal city.
The Hou Hanshu route names Aman, west of Anxi.
Reaches Sibin, beside the Tigris.
At the sea, Parthian sailors warn him the crossing can take two years, and he gives up.
Returns with reports on Da Qin's walled towns, postal relays and products.

sources.cite: Hou Hanshu ch. 88, trans. John E. Hill, Through the Jade Gate to Rome, 2009
Wikipedia, Gan Ying

name: Gandhi's life moves
what: Mohandas Gandhi moves from Porbandar to law school in London, two decades of activism in South Africa, and thirty years of campaigning across India, from Champaran and the Salt March to Noakhali and his assassination in Delhi.

legs.note: Schooled here; married to Kasturba at thirteen.
Outcast by his caste for going abroad; sails on the SS Clyde.
Studies law at the Inner Temple and joins the Vegetarian Society.
Struggles to establish a legal practice.
Arrives to work on a merchant's lawsuit.
Thrown off a first-class carriage at the station for being Indian.
Settles the lawsuit and reads Tolstoy.
Founds the Natal Indian Congress.
Fetches his family and publishes the Green Pamphlet.
Assaulted by a white mob on landing; later leads an ambulance corps in the Boer War.
Opens a law practice and starts the weekly Indian Opinion.
Founds a communal farm inspired by Ruskin's Unto This Last.
Launches satyagraha against the Asiatic registration ordinance at the Empire Theatre on 11 September 1906.
Lobbies the Colonial Office with a deputation.
Jailed several times for leading resistance to the registration act.
Houses satyagrahis' families near Johannesburg.
Leads two thousand Indian miners across the Transvaal border in defiance of the law; arrested.
Leaves South Africa after the Smuts-Gandhi agreement.
Arrives as war breaks out and organises an Indian ambulance unit.
Returns to India to a hero's welcome.
Founds his ashram.
Investigates indigo planters' abuses and defies an order to leave.
Leads the Kheda and non-cooperation campaigns from here.
Serves two years of a six-year sedition sentence.
Leaves on foot with 78 followers for the sea.
Picks up a lump of salt on the beach after a 24-day march.
Arrested at Karadi and held without trial.
Attends the Second Round Table Conference and stays in the East End at Kingsley Hall.
Meets Mussolini on his way home.
Arrested a week after landing.
Makes the village ashram his base.
Launches Quit India with 'Do or Die'; arrested next morning.
Interned; Kasturba dies here in 1944.
Walks barefoot through riot-torn villages.
Spends Independence Day fasting and spinning to calm riots.
Fasts for communal peace and is shot by Nathuram Godse.

sources.cite: M. K. Gandhi, An Autobiography, or The Story of My Experiments with Truth, Ahmedabad 1927-29
Ramachandra Guha, Gandhi Before India (2013) and Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World 1914-1948 (2018)
Wikipedia, Mahatma Gandhi

name: Hannibal's march on Italy
what: The Carthaginian general marches an army with elephants from New Carthage over the Pyrenees and Alps, destroys Roman armies at Trebia, Trasimene and Cannae, and campaigns in Italy for fifteen years before returning to Africa.

legs.note: Subdues the tribes north of the Ebro, leaving Hanno in command.
Crosses into Gaul after releasing reluctant Iberian troops.
Ferries the elephants across on rafts against hostile Volcae.
Crosses the Alps in snow in about fifteen days, losing many men; the pass is disputed.
Storms the main Taurini town after descending into Italy.
Defeats Scipio's cavalry; the consul is wounded.
Ambushes and destroys Sempronius's army in winter.
Marches four days through floods and loses an eye to infection.
Traps and annihilates Flaminius's army on the lake shore.
Rests and re-equips his army with Roman weapons.
Escapes Fabius by driving cattle with burning torches on their horns.
Winters in Apulia.
Encircles and destroys the largest Roman army yet fielded.
Capua defects to him; winters there.
Repulsed by Marcellus.
Takes the city by night through treachery, though the citadel holds out.
Marches on Rome to relieve Capua but withdraws.
Holds out in the toe of Italy and sets up his bilingual inscription at the Lacinian temple.
Lands in Africa, recalled to face Scipio.
Defeated by Scipio and Masinissa, ending the war.

sources.cite: Polybius, Histories books 3, 7-9, 15, trans. W. R. Paton, Loeb
Livy, History of Rome books 21-30
Dexter Hoyos, Hannibal's War, Oxford 2013; Adrian Goldsworthy, The Fall of Carthage, London 2000
Wikipedia, Hannibal's crossing of the Alps

name: Hasekura Tsunenaga (Keicho embassy)
what: A samurai of Date Masamune leads a Japanese embassy across the Pacific, New Spain and the Atlantic to Philip III and Pope Paul V, and returns after seven years to a Japan banning Christianity.

legs.note: Sights the California coast.
Lands in New Spain; brawls break out with Spaniards.
Received by the viceroy; many of the party are baptised.
Embarks with Sebastian Vizcaino's fleet.
Changes ships in Cuba.
Reaches Spain.
Enters the city in state.
Meets Philip III on 30 January 1615 and is baptised in February.
Sails for Italy.
Storm-driven ashore; locals record the Japanese blowing noses into paper tissues.
Lands in the Papal States.
Received by Pope Paul V on 3 November and made a Roman citizen.
Philip III declines to sign a trade agreement.
Waits for passage; some of his party stay and their descendants keep the surname Japon.
Rejoins the San Juan Bautista.
The galleon is sold to the Spanish; he waits two years.
Returns to a Japan where Christianity is banned.
Reports to Date Masamune; dies in 1622.

sources.cite: Lothar Knauth, Confrontacion transpacifica: el Japon y el Nuevo Mundo hispanico 1542-1639, Mexico 1972
Scipione Amati, Historia del regno di Voxu, Rome 1615
Wikipedia, Hasekura Tsunenaga

name: Ho Chi Minh's thirty years abroad
what: Nguyen Tat Thanh leaves Saigon as a ship's kitchen hand, works his way through France, the Americas and Britain, becomes the communist Nguyen Ai Quoc in Paris and a Comintern agent in Moscow, Canton, Siam and Hong Kong, and returns to Vietnam in 1941.

legs.note: Applies unsuccessfully to the French Colonial School.
Works as a gardener and uses the town as his base between voyages.
Arrives on the Amiral Latouche-Treville.
Writes to the colonial administration from New York; may have worked in Boston and Harlem.
Claims to work at the Carlton Hotel kitchens and on the Newhaven-Dieppe ferry.
As Nguyen Ai Quoc, petitions the Versailles peace conference for Vietnamese rights.
Votes for the Third International and becomes a founding member of the French Communist Party.
Edits Le Paria under police surveillance.
Works for the Comintern, studies at the Communist University of the Toilers of the East and attends Lenin's funeral.
Founds the Vietnamese Revolutionary Youth League and trains cadres; marries Zeng Xueming.
Returns after Chiang Kai-shek's coup; recovers from tuberculosis in the Crimea.
Brief return, then Brussels, Berlin, Switzerland and Italy.
Lands in Siam disguised as a Chinese.
Organises Vietnamese émigrés in north-eastern Siam disguised as a monk.
Chairs the meeting of 3 February 1930 that founds the Communist Party of Vietnam; arrested in June 1931.
Released after a Privy Council appeal, slips out of Hong Kong.
Studies at the Lenin School, under suspicion during the purges.
Returns to China to work with the Chinese communists.
Serves with the Eighth Route Army under Ye Jianying.
Meets Vo Nguyen Giap and Pham Van Dong.
Crosses back into Vietnam after thirty years and founds the Viet Minh in May.

sources.cite: William J. Duiker, Ho Chi Minh: A Life, New York 2000
Sophie Quinn-Judge, Ho Chi Minh: The Missing Years 1919-1941, Berkeley 2002
Wikipedia, Ho Chi Minh

name: Hyecho
what: A young Silla monk sails from China to India, walks to the Buddhist holy places, south and west India, Kashmir, Afghanistan and Persia, and returns overland to the Tang garrison at Kucha.

legs.note: First stop on the sea route.
Lands at the Bengal port.
Finds the site of the parinirvana nearly deserted.
Describes an Ashokan pillar with its lion capital.
Visits Vulture Peak.
Writes a poem at the Mahabodhi.
Visits Central India's capital and nearby Sankasya.
After three months' walk south, sees a great rock-cut monastery linked to Nagarjuna.
Two months north, notes the country half destroyed by the Arabs.
Stays briefly in North India.
Finds a devout Buddhist king and many monasteries.
Reports Tibetan rule in Great Bolor.
Finds a Turkic king patronising Buddhism.
Counts about six thousand monks under the Turk Shahi king.
Notes a strong Buddhist presence.
Last Buddhist country westwards, now under Arab rule.
A month west of Tokharistan, people know nothing of Buddhism.
Notes the Sogdians follow a fire religion.
Finds no Buddhism.
Crosses the Pamir corridor eastwards.
Reaches Tang-controlled territory.
Arrives at the Protector General's seat in the first decade of the 11th month of 727.
Returns to work with Vajrabodhi on esoteric texts.

sources.cite: Hyecho, Wang ocheonchukguk jeon, trans. Han-sung Yang et al., The Hye Ch'o Diary, Seoul 1984
Donald S. Lopez Jr., Hyecho's Journey: The World of Buddhism, Chicago 2017
Wikipedia, Hyecho

name: Ahmad ibn Fadlan
what: Secretary to the Abbasid caliph's embassy to the king of the Volga Bulghars, he crosses Iran, Khwarazm and the steppe in winter and describes the Oghuz, Bashkirs and a Rus ship funeral.

legs.note: Crosses the Zagros on the Khurasan road.
Waits several days because the Daylamite ruler controls the road.
Passes through Khurasan.
Continues to the Oxus crossing at Amul.
Meets the young Samanid emir Nasr ibn Ahmad; the promised money to fund the mission is not ready.
Winters in Khwarazm in bitter cold; camels' beards freeze.
Climbs onto the plateau in deep snow with a caravan of 3,000 horses and 5,000 men.
Negotiates passage with the Oghuz army commander.
Crosses the river in camel-skin boats; meets Pechenegs.
Fears the Bashkirs, whom he calls the most dangerous of the Turks.
Reads the caliph's letter to the Bulghar king Almish and is blamed for the missing money.
Witnesses the Rus merchants and the ship funeral of a chieftain.

sources.cite: Ibn Fadlan, Mission to the Volga, trans. James E. Montgomery, in Two Arabic Travel Books, New York University Press 2014
Ibn Fadlan and the Land of Darkness, trans. Paul Lunde and Caroline Stone, Penguin 2012
Wikipedia, Ahmad ibn Fadlan

name: Ibn Jubayr
what: An Andalusian secretary makes the hajj by Genoese ship and Red Sea dhow, praising Saladin's Egypt, then returns through Baghdad, Damascus and crusader Acre to shipwreck off Norman Sicily.

legs.note: Boards a Genoese ship bound for Alexandria.
Hears of Muslim captives sold here; a severe storm follows.
Passes the island before turning south.
Angered by customs officials; admires the Pharos lighthouse.
Visits Saladin's hospitals and colleges and sees the pyramids.
Travels up the Nile to the caravan town for the desert crossing.
Crosses the Eastern Desert to the Red Sea port.
Survives a perilous crossing on a sewn-plank jalba.
Lives eight months in Mecca and performs the hajj.
Visits the Prophet's tomb with the Iraqi pilgrim caravan.
Crosses the desert with the caravan.
Hears the preacher Ibn al-Jawzi and describes the decline of the city.
Travels up the Tigris.
Describes its citadel.
Praises the Umayyad mosque and its clock.
Notes Muslim and Christian caravans passing freely despite war.
Visits the Frankish port and its Muslim quarter.
Embarks on a Genoese ship with Christian pilgrims bound west.
Wrecked in the strait; King William II pays the fares of poor Muslims.
Describes Muslim officials at the Norman court.
Waits for a ship to Spain.
Lands in al-Andalus.
Home after two years and three months.

sources.cite: The Travels of Ibn Jubayr, trans. R. J. C. Broadhurst, London 1952
Wikipedia, Ibn Jubayr

name: Ibn Khaldun's career
what: The Tunisian historian moves between the courts of Fez, Granada, Bejaia and Tlemcen, withdraws to a desert fortress to write the Muqaddimah, and ends his life as a judge in Mamluk Cairo after meeting Timur at Damascus.

legs.note: Spends the winter among the Banu Muzni on his way west.
Serves the Marinid Abu Inan; is jailed 22 months, then becomes a minister.
Welcomed by the Nasrid Muhammad V, whom he had helped in Fez.
Negotiates a treaty with Pedro the Cruel and declines his offer to stay.
Becomes chamberlain to the Hafsid emir Abu Abdallah.
Takes refuge with the Dawawida Arabs after his patron's death.
Summoned by the new sultan; works among the Arab tribes.
Lives under the patronage of the Marinid regent.
A brief stay before being sent back to Africa.
Writes the Muqaddimah in three years of seclusion.
Completes his history in the service of the Hafsid Abu l-Abbas.
Lands, leaving Tunis on the pretext of the hajj.
Becomes professor and Maliki chief judge; his family drowns off Alexandria in 1384.
Performs the hajj.
Teaches in Cairo madrasas and is repeatedly made and unmade judge.
Lowered over the city wall by ropes to meet Timur and writes him a report on the Maghreb.
Finishes his autobiography and dies a month after his sixth appointment as judge.

Walter J. Fischel, Ibn Khaldun and Tamerlane, Berkeley 1952
Wikipedia, Ibn Khaldun

name: Ida Pfeiffer's first journey round the world
carrier: Ida Pfeiffer's first journey round the world
what: A Viennese widow in her late forties travels alone and cheaply round the world by sailing ship, caravan and riverboat through Brazil, Chile, Tahiti, China, India, Mesopotamia, Persia and the Caucasus.

legs.note: Boards the Danish brig Caroline.
Enters the harbour; attacked by a runaway slave on an excursion and fights him off.
Rounds the Horn on the barque John Renwick.
Lands in Chile.
Meets Queen Pomare IV under the new French protectorate.
Reaches the new British colony.
Walks the city streets despite hostility to foreigners.
Explores the jungle and plantations.
Visits Kandy and the Temple of the Tooth.
Sails up the Hooghly.
Watches cremations at the ghats.
Visits the Mughal court.
Crosses central India by ox-cart and palanquin, then sails for the Persian Gulf.
Steams up the Tigris from Basra.
Visits Layard's excavations at Nineveh.
Crosses Kurdistan with a caravan, the first European woman to do so.
Enters Russian territory and is briefly suspected as a spy.
Joins a caravan into Georgia.
Sails across the Black Sea.
Passes through Greece.
Returns to a city in revolution.

sources.cite: Ida Pfeiffer, Eine Frauenfahrt um die Welt, Vienna 1850; trans. A Woman's Journey Round the World, London 1852
Wikipedia, Ida Pfeiffer

name: Isabella Bird in Japan
what: The English travel writer Isabella Bird rides and walks with her young interpreter Ito through the unvisited interior of northern Honshu to the Ainu of Hokkaido, then tours the Kansai, recording it in Unbeaten Tracks in Japan.

legs.note: Stays at the British legation with Harry Parkes.
Lodges at the Kanaya house and admires the Toshogu shrines.
Takes a river boat down the Agano after a hard mountain crossing.
Visits the Church Missionary Society station.
Praises the new prefectural buildings.
Tours the hospital and normal school.
Finishes the flooded northern road and crosses the strait.
Rests among missionaries.
Lives three days among the Ainu in the chief Benri's house.
Sails back south.
Returns to the legation.
Begins a tour of the Kansai.
Stays at the Doshisha college and visits temples.
Visits the Grand Shrines.
Sees the mint and the commercial city.
Departs Japan for Hong Kong and Malaya.

sources.cite: Isabella L. Bird, Unbeaten Tracks in Japan, 2 vols, London 1880
Wikipedia, Unbeaten Tracks in Japan

name: Iwakura Mission
what: Iwakura Tomomi leads about fifty Meiji government leaders, including Okubo Toshimichi and Ito Hirobumi, plus students, on a twenty-one-month study tour of the United States and Europe to seek treaty revision and learn how the West worked.

legs.note: Feted by the city; Ito gives his 'rising sun' speech.
Snowbound for nearly three weeks on the transcontinental railroad.
Sees the city rebuilding after the great fire.
Meets President Grant; treaty talks fail for lack of full powers, and Okubo and Ito return to Japan for credentials.
Tours New England mills and schools before sailing.
Arrives on the Cunard steamer Olympus.
Visits Parliament, the Bank of England and the Crystal Palace.
Tours Scotland, including Glasgow shipyards and the Highlands.
Inspects cotton mills.
Visits Cammell's steelworks.
Audience with Queen Victoria.
Received by President Thiers on 26 December.
Visits King Leopold II.
Recalls the Dutch as Japan's old window on the West.
Bismarck tells them at dinner that international law serves the strong.
Received by Alexander II.
Visits the Danish court.
Visits King Oscar II.
Received by King Victor Emmanuel II.
Shown letters of Hasekura's 1615 embassy in the state archives.
Visits the World Exhibition, where Japan has its first pavilion.
Studies Swiss federalism and militia.
Embarks for home via Suez.
Notes European domination of the Asian ports.
Calls at the Straits port.
Last stop before Japan.
Returns nearly two years after setting out, to the Korea crisis.

Wikipedia, Iwakura Mission

name: Jose Rizal's travels
what: The Filipino ophthalmologist and novelist studies in Madrid, Paris and Heidelberg, publishes his anti-colonial novels in Berlin and Ghent, circles the world via Japan and America, and is exiled to Dapitan before his execution in Manila.

legs.note: First sight of a foreign city.
Lands via Suez after passing Aden and Naples.
Writes the essay Love of Country.
Takes degrees in medicine and philosophy at the Universidad Central.
Trains as an eye surgeon under Louis de Wecker.
Assists at the university eye clinic and writes To the Flowers of Heidelberg.
Translates Schiller's William Tell into Tagalog.
Publishes Noli Me Tangere in March 1887.
Meets his correspondent Ferdinand Blumentritt for the first time.
Ends his European tour.
Returns; opens a clinic in Calamba and treats his mother's eyes.
Leaves under pressure from friars and the governor.
Falls in love with Usui Seiko and studies Japanese theatre.
Quarantined, then crosses the United States by rail.
Sails for Liverpool.
Copies Morga's 1609 history of the Philippines in the British Museum.
Publishes his annotated Morga and visits the Exposition Universelle.
Writes El Filibusterismo.
Breaks with Marcelo del Pilar over leadership of the reform movement.
Courts Nellie Boustead.
Prints El Filibusterismo on borrowed money in September.
Practises as an eye doctor; visits Sandakan to plan a Filipino colony.
Founds La Liga Filipina on 3 July and is arrested days later.
Four years of exile: builds a school, clinic and water system.
Waits to sail as a volunteer army doctor to Cuba as the Katipunan revolt breaks out.
Arrested on arrival and shipped back.
Tried for rebellion and shot at Bagumbayan.

sources.cite: Austin Coates, Rizal: Philippine Nationalist and Martyr, Hong Kong 1968
Leon Ma. Guerrero, The First Filipino, Manila 1963
Wikipedia, Jose Rizal

name: Leo Africanus
what: A Granada-born Fez diplomat travels to Timbuktu and the eastern Mediterranean, is captured by Christian corsairs, baptised by Pope Leo X, and writes in Italy the Description of Africa.

legs.note: His family settles in Fez, where he studies at the Qarawiyyin.
Crosses the Atlas with his uncle's embassy to the Songhay.
Describes the city's scholars, judges and book trade under Askia Muhammad.
Describes the Songhay royal city and its market.
Serves the Wattasid sultan Muhammad al-Burtughali on missions in Morocco.
Carries a mission from the sultan of Fez to the Ottoman court.
Is in the port during the Ottoman conquest of Mamluk Egypt.
Sees the city just after Selim I's conquest.
Travels up the Nile before crossing to the Red Sea.
Probably performs the pilgrimage.
Captured at sea by Spanish corsairs and held by the Knights Hospitaller.
Presented to Leo X, imprisoned in Castel Sant'Angelo, then baptised in St Peter's in 1520.
Writes an Arabic-Hebrew-Latin medical vocabulary for Jacob Mantino.
Finishes his manuscript on African geography under Clement VII.
Probably leaves Italy before the Sack of Rome and returns to Islam in Tunis.

sources.cite: Natalie Zemon Davis, Trickster Travels: A Sixteenth-Century Muslim Between Worlds, New York 2006
Leo Africanus, Description of Africa, ed. G. B. Ramusio, Venice 1550
Wikipedia, Leo Africanus

name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
what: The Corps of Discovery under Meriwether Lewis and William Clark ascends the Missouri, winters with the Mandan, crosses the Rockies with Sacagawea's help, reaches the Pacific and returns to St Louis.

legs.note: Lewis joins from St Louis.
Camps at the site of Kansas City.
First council with Oto and Missouria leaders.
Sergeant Charles Floyd dies, probably of appendicitis.
A tense standoff with the Lakota.
Winters with the Mandan and Hidatsa; hires Charbonneau and Sacagawea.
Reaches the mouth of the Yellowstone.
Portages eighteen miles round five waterfalls.
Names the Jefferson, Madison and Gallatin rivers; Sacagawea recognises her childhood homeland.
Lewis crosses the Continental Divide.
Sacagawea finds her brother Cameahwait is the Shoshone chief; buys horses.
Prepares to cross the Bitterroots on the Lolo Trail.
Starving, the party is fed by the Nez Perce.
Builds dugout canoes.
Portages the great fishing falls of the Columbia.
Reaches the Pacific; the whole party, including York and Sacagawea, votes on where to winter.
A wet winter of elk meat and map-making.
Waits with the Nez Perce for snow to melt.
The captains split to explore separately.
Clark carves his name on the sandstone butte.
Lewis's party kills two Blackfeet in the expedition's only deadly fight.
The two parties reunite.
Leaves Charbonneau, Sacagawea and their son.
Returns after two years and four months, long given up for dead.

name: Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation
what: A Spanish fleet of five ships under Ferdinand Magellan finds the strait at the tip of South America and crosses the Pacific; after Magellan's death at Mactan, Elcano brings the Victoria home round Africa, completing the first circumnavigation.

legs.note: Waits at the river mouth, then puts to sea.
Takes on supplies in the Canaries.
Trades with the Tupi and executes a sodomy convict.
Explores the estuary, hoping it is the passage.
Winters here and crushes a mutiny of three captains on 1-2 April.
Waits after the Santiago is wrecked nearby.
Sights the entrance of the strait.
Exits into the ocean he names Pacific; the San Antonio has deserted.
Reaches land after 98 days of starvation and scurvy.
First landfall in the Philippines.
Holds an Easter mass and makes blood brotherhood with Rajah Kolambu.
Rajah Humabon and hundreds of Cebuanos are baptised.
Magellan is killed fighting Lapulapu's warriors.
Humabon turns on the Spaniards and kills about 27 at a banquet.
Burns the Concepcion for lack of crew.
Takes on food after wandering in the islands.
Received by the sultan with elephants.
Loads cloves; the leaking Trinidad stays behind.
Last stop before the Indian Ocean crossing.
Rounds the cape with only rice to eat.
Finds the ship's log is a day behind; thirteen men are seized by the Portuguese.
Elcano returns with eighteen men in the Victoria.
The survivors walk barefoot to give thanks at the shrine of Santa Maria de la Victoria.
Elcano is received by Charles V and granted a coat of arms showing a globe.

name: Matteo Ricci
what: An Italian Jesuit trained in mathematics sails to Goa and Macau, works his way north through Ming China in scholar's robes over eighteen years, and becomes the first European allowed to live in Beijing.

legs.note: Studies Portuguese while waiting for the India fleet.
Sails on the Sao Luis.
Teaches and is ordained in Cochin in 1580.
Studies Chinese at Valignano's order.
Builds a mission house and displays his world map.
Meets the scholar Qu Rukui and adopts the dress of a Confucian literatus.
Writes his treatise on friendship and befriends Ming princes.
First attempt on the southern capital.
Fails to gain an audience and leaves after two months.
Winters in the Yangtze delta.
Debates Buddhist monks and meets Xu Guangqi.
Detained for months by the eunuch Ma Tang.
Presents clocks to the Wanli emperor, translates Euclid with Xu Guangqi and dies here.

name: The Mozart family grand tour
what: Leopold Mozart takes his prodigy children Nannerl and Wolfgang on a three-and-a-half-year concert tour through the German courts, Paris, London and the Dutch Republic, returning home via Switzerland.

legs.note: The children play before Elector Maximilian III.
Three concerts in Leopold's home town; his mother stays away.
Amaze Elector Palatine Karl Theodor at his summer court.
Three concerts earn 200 florins.
Public concerts attended by the young Goethe.
Travel down the Rhine by riverboat.
Continue via Bonn.
Play for Princess Anna Amalia of Prussia, who pays in kisses.
Wait weeks for Prince Charles of Lorraine; grand concert on 7 November.
Lodge with the Bavarian ambassador; Grimm promotes the children.
Attend a royal dinner at court.
Publish Wolfgang's first sonatas and give concerts.
Play for George III and Queen Charlotte four days after arriving.
Leopold convalesces; Wolfgang writes his first symphony.
Befriends J. C. Bach and is examined by Daines Barrington.
Wolfgang's tonsillitis and Leopold's dizziness delay them a month.
Wolfgang plays the new organ at the Bernardine chapel.
Wolfgang plays the cathedral organ.
Guests of Princess Carolina; Nannerl nearly dies of typhoid.
Public concerts.
Celebrate the installation of William V of Orange on 11 March.
Concert before leaving the Netherlands.
Second stay; Grimm notes Wolfgang's growth as composer.
Concert for the Prince of Conti with a 'very mediocre' local orchestra.
Concerts before heading to Switzerland.
Two concerts; meet the composer Gretry.
Perform for local nobility.
Concerts at the Collegium Musicum.
Twelve days with Prince Fuerstenberg.
Wolfgang falls ill, then plays for the Elector on 22 November.
Home to the Getreidegasse.

Stanley Sadie, Mozart: The Early Years 1756-1781, Oxford 2006
Wikipedia, Mozart family grand tour

name: Mungo Park's first expedition
what: A young Scottish surgeon sent by the African Association walks from the Gambia to the Niger at Segou, survives captivity by the Moors and fever, and returns on a slave ship after two and a half years.

legs.note: Reaches the Gambia river.
Learns Mandinka at Dr Laidley's trading post and survives fever.
Received by the king of Wuli.
The almami takes his best coat.
The king of Kaarta advises him to go through Ludamar.
Held prisoner by the Moorish chief Ali and mocked by his court.
Escapes from Ali's camp with only his horse and compass.
Sees the Niger 'glittering to the morning sun' flowing eastward.
Exhausted and penniless, turns back.
Follows the Niger upstream.
Nursed through fever by the slave trader Karfa Taura and waits out the rains.
Walks back with Karfa's slave coffle and is greeted as one risen from the dead.
The American slaver Charlestown, leaking, puts in at the West Indies.
Lands in England.
Reaches London on Christmas morning.

name: Napoleon's Egyptian campaign
what: General Bonaparte sails from Toulon with an army and a commission of scholars, seizes Malta and Egypt, invades Syria as far as Acre, and slips back to France to seize power.

legs.note: Takes the island from the Knights of St John.
Lands and storms the city.
Repulses Mamluk cavalry on the Nile.
Defeats Murad Bey's Mamluks in the Battle of the Pyramids.
Founds the Institut d'Egypte; learns of Nelson's destruction of his fleet at Aboukir.
Explores traces of the ancient canal and nearly drowns in the Red Sea tide.
Prepares the invasion of Syria.
Takes the fort after crossing Sinai.
Occupies the town.
Storms the town and has some 3,000 prisoners shot; plague breaks out.
Besieges the city held by Jazzar Pasha with Sidney Smith's help.
Rescues Kleber's division from an Ottoman relief army.
Fails to storm the walls and lifts the two-month siege.
Retreats, reportedly ordering plague victims poisoned.
Stages a triumphal entry to mask the defeat.
Destroys an Ottoman landing army.
Secretly sails for France, leaving Kleber in command.
Last visit to his birthplace, held by contrary winds.
Lands without observing quarantine.
Overthrows the Directory in the coup of 18 Brumaire.

name: Napoleon's Russian campaign
what: Napoleon leads the Grande Armee of some 600,000 men across the Niemen to Moscow and back, losing most of it to battle, hunger, cold and the crossing of the Berezina, then races ahead by sledge to Paris.

legs.note: Holds court for the allied German kings and the Austrian emperor.
Passes through Poland.
Inspects the assembling corps.
Oversees supply depots for the invasion.
The army crosses into Russia on pontoon bridges without a declaration.
Enters the city abandoned by Alexander I; heat and dysentery thin the ranks.
Pauses, debating whether to go on.
Storms the burning city as the Russians retreat.
Wins the bloodiest day of the war at a cost of some 30,000 men.
Enters an empty city that is set on fire; waits in vain for peace terms.
Kutuzov blocks the southern route, forcing a retreat along the devastated road.
The rearguard is mauled as snow begins.
Finds the depots looted; frost reaches minus 20.
Fights through Russian blocking forces.
Burns surplus baggage and the pontoon train to move faster.
Dutch pontonniers build bridges in icy water; tens of thousands are lost in the crossing.
Hands command to Murat and leaves by sledge.
Tells the Abbe de Pradt there is only one step from the sublime to the ridiculous.
Passes through incognito.
Arrives near midnight to shore up his rule.

name: Olaudah Equiano
what: Kidnapped as a child from Igboland, Equiano is enslaved in Virginia, at sea in the Seven Years' War and in the Caribbean, buys his freedom, sails to the Arctic and the Mosquito Coast, and becomes Britain's leading Black abolitionist author.

Survives the Middle Passage with 244 other captives.

Sees snow for the first time in England.
Serves with Pascal at the siege on HMS Namur.
Baptised at St Margaret's, Westminster.
With Boscawen's fleet in the Mediterranean.
Fights in the battle of Lagos against the French.

Wrecked on the Nancy.
Settles in England and works as a hairdresser and seaman.
Voyages to the Levant.
Sails with the Phipps Arctic expedition on HMS Racehorse, working with Dr Charles Irving.
Manages enslaved labourers on Irving's failed plantation.
Returns to England.
Joins the abolitionist movement and tells Granville Sharp of the Zong massacre in 1783.
Commissary for the Sierra Leone resettlement ships; dismissed after exposing fraud.
Publishes The Interesting Narrative by subscription.
Sells nearly two thousand copies on a book tour of Ireland.
Marries Susannah Cullen.
Promotes a new edition in Scotland.
Dies in Westminster.

Vincent Carretta, Equiano, the African: Biography of a Self-Made Man, Athens GA 2005

what: Powhatan's daughter moves between her father's towns and English Jamestown, is taken captive, marries John Rolfe, and is sent to London as the Virginia Company's showpiece, dying at Gravesend on the voyage home.

Instructed in Christianity by Alexander Whitaker and baptised Rebecca.

Shown to London society by the Virginia Company.
Moves out of the smoky city; meets John Smith again and turns away from him.
Presented to King James at Ben Jonson's masque The Vision of Delight.
Falls ill on the ship home and is buried at St George's church.

name: Pytheas of Massalia

Names the south-eastern corner of Britain, completing the island's triangle.

Returns and writes On the Ocean.

Obtains a safe-conduct from Kaidu.
Rests at a monastery near Tus.
Meets the Patriarch Mar Denha.
Visits the patriarchal church and shrines.
Turns back from Syria because the roads are unsafe.

Sent by Ilkhan Arghun with letters and gifts for the Christian rulers.
Takes ship on the Black Sea.

Winters in the city.

Visit the university.
Spend Christmas.
Embark for Italy.
Land in Tuscany.
Guests of Grand Duke Francesco I de' Medici.

Pilgrimage to the Holy House.
Arrive by riverboat from Ferrara amid great acclaim.

name: Timur's campaigns
what: From his enthronement at Balkh, the Turco-Mongol conqueror campaigns for thirty-five years across Iran, the Golden Horde steppe, India, Syria and Anatolia, returning between wars to Samarkand, and dies marching on China.

legs.note: Makes Samarkand his capital and begins fortifying it.
Takes the Khwarazmian capital after a siege.
The Kart ruler surrenders the city.
Campaigns in Sistan and takes Kandahar.
Occupies the city after Tokhtamysh's sack.
Massacres the population after a revolt and builds towers of skulls.
The Muzaffarid city submits.
After a march deep into the steppe, defeats Tokhtamysh's Golden Horde.
Returns before the five-year campaign west.
Defeats and kills Shah Mansur, ending the Muzaffarids.
Takes the city as the Jalayirid Ahmad flees to Egypt.
Defeats Tokhtamysh decisively in the North Caucasus.
Takes the Ryazan frontier town, then turns back before Moscow.
Destroys the Golden Horde capital and Astrakhan.
Builds the Aq Saray at Shahrisabz and gardens around Samarkand.
Crosses the Indus to invade the Delhi Sultanate.
Defeats Sultan Nasir al-Din Mahmud and sacks the city.
Begins the Bibi Khanum mosque with Indian booty.
Sacks the Ottoman city and buries its defenders alive.
Defeats the Mamluk governors and sacks the city.
Besieges and burns the city; questions the historian Ibn Khaldun.
Storms the city and orders mass killings.
Defeats and captures the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I.
Takes the Hospitallers' castle.
Receives the Castilian envoy Clavijo amid feasts.
Dies of illness in winter quarters on the way to invade Ming China.

sources.cite: Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane, Cambridge 1989
Sharaf al-Din Ali Yazdi, Zafarnama (1424-25); Ibn Arabshah, Tamerlane, trans. J. H. Sanders, London 1936
Ruy Gonzalez de Clavijo, Embassy to Tamerlane 1403-1406, trans. Guy Le Strange, London 1928

name: Tupaia
what: An arioi priest and navigator from Ra'iatea, exiled to Tahiti, joins the Endeavour, steers it through the Society and Austral islands, draws a chart of the Pacific and interprets for Cook in New Zealand before dying at Batavia.

legs.note: Becomes adviser and partner of the chiefess Purea; meets Samuel Wallis in 1767.
Befriends Joseph Banks during the transit of Venus and asks to sail with the Endeavour.
Pilots the ship through the reef passage.
Returns home with the British and conducts ceremonies at the marae.
Begins his chart of some 74 islands around this time.
Finds he can speak with Maori in a related language.
Debates with tohunga; his drawings and a cave there are remembered locally.
Interprets during trade.
His fame spreads among Maori.
Questions Maori about their origins and Hawaiki.
Cannot understand the Gweagal language.
Fishes and gathers greens to fight his scurvy.
Dies of fever after his young assistant Taiata.

sources.cite: Anne Salmond, Aphrodite's Island: The European Discovery of Tahiti, Berkeley 2009
Joan Druett, Tupaia: Captain Cook's Polynesian Navigator, Santa Barbara 2011
The Endeavour Journal of Joseph Banks 1768-1771, ed. J. C. Beaglehole, Sydney 1962

name: Vasco da Gama's first voyage
what: A Portuguese fleet of four ships rounds the Cape of Good Hope, works up the Swahili coast and crosses the Indian Ocean with a Malindi pilot to Calicut, returning after a disastrous scurvy-ridden crossing.

legs.note: Takes on water and meat before the long swing into the South Atlantic.
First landfall after three months at sea; skirmish with Khoikhoi.
Rounds the cape.
Trades with Khoikhoi herders and breaks up the storeship.
Names the coast Natal for Christmas.
Rests a month while scurvy strikes the crews.
Meets Muslim merchants and the sultan; relations sour.
Met with hostility and leaves.
The sultan supplies a Gujarati pilot for the crossing.
Lands and negotiates with the Zamorin, whose court finds his gifts paltry.
Careens the ships before sailing west.
Sights Africa after a three-month crossing that kills half the crew.
Recovers; the Sao Rafael is later burned for lack of hands.
Passes south again.
Rounds the cape homeward.
Coelho's Berrio separates and sails straight for Lisbon.
His brother Paulo da Gama dies here.
Arrives on an Azorean caravel (29 August per Barros; other sources say September).

sources.cite: A Journal of the First Voyage of Vasco da Gama 1497-1499 (Roteiro), trans. E. G. Ravenstein, Hakluyt Society 1898
Sanjay Subrahmanyam, The Career and Legend of Vasco da Gama, Cambridge 1997

name: William of Rubruck
what: A Flemish Franciscan sent informally by Louis IX crosses the Pontic and Kazakh steppes by cart and horse to Mongke Khan's court and Karakorum, then returns through the Caucasus and Anatolia.

legs.note: Lands in the Crimea and buys ox-carts for the steppe.
Crosses the Don by ferry among Mongol post stations.
Sartaq, rumoured to be Christian, sends him on to his father Batu.
Batu refuses to let him stay and sends him to the Great Khan.
Rides east on horseback across the steppe of the Qangli.
Reaches the mountains south of the steppe and turns east.
Stays twelve days and debates with Buddhist monks.
Passes a great lake with an island, buffeted by winds through a pass.
Received by Mongke Khan on 4 January 1254.
Describes the city's quarters, the silver tree fountain of Guillaume Boucher and a religious debate.
Spends two weeks with Batu on the return.
Passes the newly built Mongol town on the Volga.
Goes through the Iron Gate between the Caucasus and the Caspian.
Spends Christmas in the city devastated by the Mongols.
Crosses Seljuk Anatolia.
Embarks for Cyprus.
Arrives in the crusader county and writes his report for Louis IX.

sources.cite: The Mission of Friar William of Rubruck, trans. Peter Jackson with David Morgan, Hakluyt Society 1990
Wikipedia, William of Rubruck

name: Xu Xiake's southwest journey
what: A Ming gentleman-geographer from Jiangyin spends four years walking through Jiangxi, Hunan, Guangxi, Guizhou and Yunnan, recording karst caves and river sources, until illness forces him to be carried home.

legs.note: Travels south through Zhejiang.
Crosses Jiangxi by river and mountain paths.
Climbs the Southern Sacred Mountain; later robbed of his belongings on the Xiang river.
Explores and measures the karst caves around the city.
Continues through Guangxi.
His companion Jingwen dies on the road.
Enters Guizhou.
Describes the great waterfall on the Baishui river.
Reaches Yunnan and explores Dian lake.
Buries Jingwen's ashes at the Buddhist mountain as promised.
Guest of the Naxi chief Mu Zeng.
Visits Erhai lake and the marble quarries.
Reaches the far south-western frontier and its volcanic springs.
Writes the mountain's gazetteer as his legs fail him.
Carried home by order of the Lijiang chief; dies there in March 1641.

sources.cite: Julian Ward, Xu Xiake (1587-1641): The Art of Travel Writing, Richmond 2001
Li Chi, The Travel Diaries of Hsu Hsia-k'o, Hong Kong 1974
Wikipedia, Xu Xiake

name: Yijing
what: A Tang monk sails to India on a Persian ship, studies ten years at Nalanda, and spends years translating in Srivijaya before returning to Empress Wu's Luoyang with some 400 texts.

legs.note: Boards a Persian merchant ship in the eleventh month.
Spends six months learning Sanskrit grammar.
Stays two months.
Changes ship for India.
Trades with islanders he calls the 'naked people'.
Lands in the second month of 673 and studies Sanskrit for a year.
Travels with the monk Dachengdeng and merchants to the holy sites.
Studies for about ten years at the great monastery.
Leaves India by sea with his manuscripts.
Returns through the Straits.
Translates and writes his Record of Buddhist Practices.
Goes ashore to recruit helpers and get paper and ink, then sails back.
Completes his translations and memoirs of Chinese pilgrim monks.
Returns to China for good.
Welcomed by Empress Wu Zetian with some 400 texts.

sources.cite: I-Tsing, A Record of the Buddhist Religion as Practised in India and the Malay Archipelago (AD 671-695), trans. J. Takakusu, Oxford 1896
Yijing, Chinese Monks in India (Da Tang Xiyu qiufa gaoseng zhuan), trans. Latika Lahiri, Delhi 1986

name: Zhang Qian
what: A Han court officer sent west to seek an alliance with the Yuezhi spends years as a Xiongnu captive, reaches Ferghana and Bactria, and returns with China's first report of Central Asia.

legs.note: Crosses out of Han territory through Longxi into Xiongnu-controlled land.
Held captive for about ten years; marries a Xiongnu wife and has a son.
Escapes west and is welcomed by the king of Dayuan, who has heard of Han wealth.
Dayuan provides guides and interpreters to Kangju, which passes him on to the Yuezhi.
Finds the Yuezhi settled and unwilling to fight the Xiongnu.
Sees the Bactrian market and cloth and bamboo from Shu, implying a route via India.
Returns along the southern mountains to avoid the Xiongnu but is captured again.
Held over a year until the chanyu's death and civil strife let him flee.
Returns with his wife and Ganfu only, after about thirteen years, and reports to Emperor Wu.
Directs envoys south-west through the Yi peoples to seek a road to India; all are blocked.
Sets out with three hundred men and great herds and silks for the Wusun.
Proposes an alliance and sends deputies on to Dayuan, Kangju, Yuezhi, Daxia and Anxi.
Returns with Wusun envoys and horses; dies about a year later.

sources.cite: Sima Qian, Shiji ch. 123 (Account of Dayuan), trans. Burton Watson, Records of the Grand Historian: Han Dynasty II, Columbia 1993
